summary.headline: Electronics Mart Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% to INR 2,419 crore and PAT to INR 121 crore, with reported EBITDA margin at 9.9%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's strongest quarter to date, driven by a strong AC season, healthy footfalls and conversions, and 34.2% same-store sales growth. Gross margin expanded to 17.2% from 14.6%, aided by cooling-product mix and temporary price-increase gains in IT hardware. Working capital days fell to 42 from 73 and working capital borrowings dropped to INR 97 crore from INR 658 crore at the start of the quarter. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% and a post-Ind AS EBITDA margin of 7.5-8%, and said the margin tailwinds are partly temporary.

segments.name: Large appliances
segments.commentary: 48% of revenue, led by air conditioners, with traction in washing machines and refrigerators. AC season was the best quarter yet by volume and value.

segments.name: Mobile phones
segments.commentary: 39% of revenue in Q1 FY27, down from 40% in the comparable base, as cooling-product mix rose seasonally.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +40% YoY with EBITDA margin of 10.9%. Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).

segments.name: North cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +29% YoY with record EBITDA margin of 4.9%. Management said North market for cooling products was negative versus 2024.

segments.name: Store maturity
segments.commentary: 96 stores older than 4 years run at 11.2% EBITDA margin; 131 stores under 4 years old delivered 8.1%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20% YoY, described as 'very easily achievable'; upside possible if Q4 season is strong. Management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore revenue.
FY27 full-year gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, below the Q1 level, as Q1 benefited from temporary price-increase gains.
Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at 7.5-8% for FY27; management called 9% 'too optimistic'.
Finance cost expected to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.
Plan to open 25-30 stores in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores by Diwali and 10-12 by end-Q4 FY27; 8-10 NCR stores in FY27 and about 5 South stores.
West Bengal capex about INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over the next two years, funded from internal accruals.
risks_watch: Gross margin tailwind from temporary price-increase gains in laptops and mobiles may reverse; management guides FY27 gross margin to 15-15.5%.
Delhi NCR same-store sales weak as North cooling-product market declined; management expects improvement but gave no quarterly figures.
Memory-chip shortages may force higher stock levels (50-60 days instead of 30) for some IT and mobile SKUs.
Management could not quantify the share of inventory bought at lower prior-year cost, so the gross margin benefit is hard to isolate.
Quality of the Q1 base: the comparison is against a weak AC season in Q1 FY26, so the growth rate may not persist.
New store ramp in West Bengal and North; execution against 25-30 openings a year and the 10-12 Kolkata target by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What are full-year FY27 revenue and gross margin targets, given the weak base?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth of 18-20% is described as very easily achievable; management declined to commit to INR 10,000 crore. FY27 gross margin guided at 15-15.5%, with Q1's 17.2% partly temporary from price-increase gains.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin expansion and is the benefit sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher cooling-product mix and buying laptops and mobiles at lower prices during price rises; it called the price-increase gain temporary and could not quantify the low-cost inventory share.

qa_highlights.question: Is post-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 8-9% achievable and what is the finance cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 9% is too optimistic and 7.5-8% is easily achievable; finance cost to be at least INR 10 crore lower than last year's ~INR 150 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Delhi NCR SSG weak and what store openings are planned there and in Kolkata?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the North cooling market declined versus 2024 and the base was small; Kolkata has 5 stores by Diwali and 10-12 by March 2027; NCR 8-10 stores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Capex requirement for West Bengal and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crore for stores plus about INR 50 crore for property purchases over two years, all funded from internal accruals; about 30 stores in Kolkata over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company quantify its market share gains and volume versus price contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share gains estimated at 4% to 12% outside Hyderabad depending on the geography; growth attributed mainly to volume, with ASP up only in limited categories.

capex_capacity: Plans 25-30 store openings in FY27 across existing geographies and West Bengal; 5 Kolkata stores operational by Diwali and 10-12 by 31 March 2027; 8-10 NCR stores this financial year (two opening that week in Saket and Gurgaon, 3-4 under construction); about 5 South stores.

West Bengal capex of about INR 100 crore (plus or minus INR 5-10 crore) for stores plus about INR 50 crore for buying about 11 properties in Kolkata over the next two years, transactions possibly in Q1-Q2 FY28; all funded from internal accruals.

Per-store economics: about INR 2,500 per sq ft capex on a 10,000 sq ft store (about INR 2.5 crore) plus about INR 2 crore inventory; payback under 10-11 months in South and 16-18 months in North; breakeven 30-40 days in South and about 2-2.5 months in North.
Store opex targets: rent under 3% of revenue initially, manpower and marketing each under 1%, total store opex 8-10%; SSG targeted at 10-12% from year three.
Management said it will not commit to inorganic or rapid expansion and no franchise model; all stores are company-owned and company-operated on leased properties.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 SSG 34.2%; South cluster revenue +40% with 10.9% EBITDA margin; Andhra Pradesh revenue +62% (SSG 49.1%), Telangana up-country +48% (SSG 40%), Hyderabad city +34% (SSG 32.3%).
North cluster revenue +29% with 4.9% EBITDA margin; management said the North cooling-product market declined versus 2024, and Delhi NCR SSG was weak.

Management said the Andhra Pradesh AC unit volume was about 26,000-27,000 in the first six months against about 20,000 a year earlier with a similar store count; claimed market share gains of 4% to 12% in existing clusters outside Hyderabad.

Price gains were concentrated in laptops and mobiles due to chipset/memory shortages; TVs, refrigerators, washing machines and ACs saw single-digit price hikes. Gains were periodic, not across all brands or the full 90 days.
Bill cuts grew about 36% while ASP grew about 2%, per an analyst's read; management attributed this to volume growth and low-ticket accessories and audio.

Mobile share fell to 39% from 40% on seasonal cooling-product mix; management expects mix to normalise by year-end within 1-2%. Management expects the North to trend toward South margins as stores mature.
Management said it expects memory-chip shortages may require 50-60 days stock instead of 30 days for some IT and mobile SKUs, not across all categories.
key_quotes: I am delighted to share that Q1 FY27 has been our strongest quarter to date with all the key metrics moving decisively in the right direction.
But that is a temporary upside.
It will be too optimistic. 9% means too optimistic.
So no inorganic expansion, no rapid expansion. It will be all calculated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q1 result and South momentum, but guarded on sustainability: management called the price-driven margin gain temporary, declined to commit to a INR 10,000 crore revenue target, and was evasive on the exact low-cost inventory benefit.
